habitat: Eastern coastal and littoral bush, and inland along rivers. It nests in reeds and trees.
summary: A common resident. Both sexes are all-yellow, and the bill is dark. It is the palest yellow weaver, slightly greener above when not breeding, with a stubby bill and a red eye. The immature resembles the female, and the female was otherwise not described. The call is a harsh zik and a soft swizzling. Avibase marks it rare or accidental in Kruger, so the months are unset. The Kemp paper name Yellow Weaver and the code VB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Holub’s Golden Weaver has an orange wash from the chin to the upper breast. Eastern Golden Weaver is the palest yellow, with a red eye and a stubby dark bill.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident. Avibase lists it as African Golden-Weaver and marks it rare or accidental in Kruger, so the months are unset. The female was not described apart from the shared yellow plumage. The Kruger photograph is distant and does not show the red eye. No flight photograph was found. The grade A recording is from the Eastern Cape. Population figures and the Kemp name Yellow Weaver were left unchanged.
